_about: Published artifacts are immutable: a defective build can never be removed, only superseded by a higher build number and/or neutralised. This list is the single record of every build known to be defective, in BOTH formats, keyed by subdir and then by exact artifact filename. It is not merely documentation -- three things read it. tools/make_repodata.py drops a listed .conda from repodata IF a fresh solve can still reach it -- that is, unless a higher-numbered build of the same cell (itself not known-bad) supersedes it, or an unsatisfiable constrain neutralises it. Conda has no yank, so removal is the only statement available; but a build nothing can select is better left listed, so the channel and this file agree about what exists. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Defective builds: reachability, not policy'. tools/generate_index.py YANKS a listed .whl per PEP 592, which keeps it downloadable for anyone who pinned that exact filename while stopping any resolver from selecting it, and surfaces 'reason' to the user. tools/check_lock.py reads it self-serve, for someone holding a lockfile that already pinned one. In every case the release ASSET stays byte-for-byte where it was: what changes is what a new resolve can arrive at. 'fixed_by' names the superseding build to re-lock onto.

torchvision-0.23.0-cuda128_torch28_py312.reason: Built without the jpeg, webp and nvjpeg codecs while its run deps claim them. Upstream's detection looks under TORCHVISION_INCLUDE / TORCHVISION_LIBRARY, which pointed at %PREFIX%\include on win-64 -- a conda prefix keeps that tree under %PREFIX%\Library. Detection failing is not a build failure upstream: it warns, ships an image extension without the codec, and leaves run_exports declaring it. Measured after the fact from the .pyd's PE import table, which lists libpng16.dll and nothing for jpeg, webp or nvjpeg. torchvision.io.decode_jpeg raises at runtime on this build.

torchvision-0.23.0+cu128torch2.8-cp312-c.reason: built without jpeg/webp/nvjpeg; superseded by build 2
torchvision-0.23.0+cu128torch2.8-cp312-c.detail: The wheel from the same compile as torchvision-0.23.0-cuda128_torch28_py312_h6651153_1.conda, and defective for the same reason: TORCHVISION_INCLUDE/TORCHVISION_LIBRARY pointed at %PREFIX%\include on win-64, where a conda prefix keeps that tree under %PREFIX%\Library, so upstream's codec detection found nothing and built the image extension without it. torchvision.io.decode_jpeg raises at runtime.
